protocol.name: neferwl_capture_v1
protocol.copyright: neferwl private protocol. Not for other compositors; no stability promise beyond the version of the interface.

description.summary: private capture sessions for the neferwl screen recorder

protocol.description:
Lets one client (the capture connection) open a session on a workspace and lets a second connection of the same user (the HUD) attach layer surfaces to it. While the session is active, the attached surfaces stay visible over a fullscreen window and are left out of the captures the capture connection takes (ext-image-copy-capture / wlr-screencopy on the same connection). Every other client's captures still show them.
Only one session is live in the compositor. The session token is a secret: it is sent only to the session's owner and must never be logged. Only the compositor's own user may use this protocol.

interface.name: neferwl_capture_manager_v1
interface.description: Global. Binding it starts the workspace inventory: one workspace event per workspace, then workspace events again for every change and workspace_removed for each workspace that disappears.

entry.name: invalid_output
entry.summary: the wl_output is unknown or gone

entry.name: surface_role
entry.summary: the surface is not a wlr-layer-shell surface

entry.name: invalid_layer
entry.summary: the layer is neither top nor overlay

entry.name: exclusive_keyboard
entry.summary: the layer takes the keyboard exclusively

entry.name: invalid_surface
entry.summary: the surface belongs to another client or is already mapped

request.name: destroy
request.description: Sessions created through it stay alive.

request.name: begin_session
request.description:
Asks for a session. Workspace 0 (both halves) targets the output: whatever it shows, bars and margins included, and the overview too. A non-zero workspace ID (from a workspace event) targets that workspace's frame, without bars, whether or not it is on screen and whatever the overview shows. The session is stopped with workspace_gone when the workspace is removed.
The region is in output-local logical pixels, clipped to the output (workspace 0) or to the workspace frame. A zero width or height means all of it. Record non-zero asks for the native recording border, drawn inside the target's edge and never in this connection's clean captures.
A served session answers with state, which carries the token. A session that cannot be served gets stopped with the reason, without a state. Only one session is live: a second one is stopped with reason busy.

request.name: attach_surface

description.summary: attach a layer surface to a session by token

request.description:
Marks a layer surface of this client as part of the session that owns the token, and creates the attachment object that reports the result. The client is usually not the session's owner but has the same user ID; both are checked with the peer credentials. The surface must already have the wlr-layer-shell role, on the top or overlay layer, must not have mapped yet and must not have asked for exclusive keyboard interactivity. At most 4 layers per session. Once attached, a layer never gets keyboard interactivity, whatever it asks for, and if it later moves to another layer the compositor closes it and sends detached.
The attachment answers with exactly one of attached or failed. The surface is excluded from clean captures from this request on, before it can map; attached only says that the compositor core confirmed it, and the client must not show the surface before it. A refusal is failed, not a protocol error, except the errors above.
The attachment ends with detached when the session stops or the layer surface is destroyed. Destroying the attachment object does not release the surface: it stays excluded until its layer role is destroyed or the session stops.

event.name: workspace
event.description: A workspace of the inventory, new or changed. The rectangle is the workspace frame in output-local logical pixels. Active is non-zero for the workspace on screen. Name is the workspace name or its number.

interface.name: neferwl_capture_layer_v1

description.summary: a layer surface attached to a capture session

interface.description: Created by attach_surface. Exactly one of attached or failed comes first; detached comes at most once, after attached.

entry.name: unknown_token
entry.summary: no live session has this token

entry.name: unauthorized
entry.summary: peer credentials differ from the compositor user's or are unreadable

entry.name: too_many_layers
entry.summary: the session already has the maximum of 4 attached layers

entry.name: session_ended
entry.summary: the session stopped before core confirmed the layer

entry.name: layer_destroyed
entry.summary: the layer role was destroyed before core confirmed it

entry.name: session_ended
entry.summary: the session stopped; the compositor closed the layer surface

request.name: destroy
request.description: The surface stays excluded from clean captures until its layer role is destroyed or the session stops.

event.name: attached

description.summary: the layer is part of the session

event.description: The compositor core confirmed the attachment: the layer is excluded from the session's clean captures, and was already before it could map. Safe to show.

event.name: detached
event.description: Sent once after attached. When the session stopped, the compositor also closed the layer surface (zwlr_layer_surface_v1.closed): the client destroys it.

interface.name: neferwl_capture_session_v1
interface.description: Destroying the session stops it. A session whose owner sends no ping for 5 seconds is stopped by the compositor.

entry.name: too_many_excluded
entry.summary: attached layers and their popups exceed 128 surfaces

request.name: ping
request.description: Must arrive at least every 5 seconds.

event.name: state
event.description: Sent once the session exists and on every change. The token is 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters (32 random bytes): a secret for the owner only, never logged, valid until stopped. The rectangle is the clipped target in output-local logical pixels and the workspace is the real one (0 for an output target). Active non-zero means captures of this connection are served clean. Active is 1 while the session lives: a session that is lost is stopped, never paused. The revision (64 bits, from 1) grows whenever the session's configuration changes: layers, popups, target.

event.name: stopped
event.description: Final. The token is void, the attached layers are ordinary again. Destroy the object.
